accepted_units.context_note: For fixed noncommuting translation operators, the source first chooses one solution of the covariance equations and then identifies every other solution as that base solution plus operators in the common commutant. In the explicit two-dimensional module, the commutant is generated by another pair of noncommuting operators and is itself a noncommutative torus whose parameter is related by a fractional-linear transformation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The explicit realization uses a Schwartz-function module on a continuous-discrete product, coprime integer data, chosen generators, and formula-sensitive phase conventions. The assertion that the displayed generators exhaust the commutant is stated rather than proved locally, and the interpretation as a dual torus is specific to this module.
accepted_units.title: Parameterize all solutions by the commutant of the constraints
accepted_units.why_material: This is a reusable structural move: solve an inhomogeneous constraint once, compute the algebra of operators invisible to the fixed symmetry action, and recognize the residual degrees of freedom as an affine space modeled on that commutant.

accepted_units.context_note: The source begins noncommutative geometry from the duality between a compact space and its commutative function algebra, then transports geometric roles algebraically: vector bundles become finitely generated projective modules, derivations play directions, connections satisfy a Leibniz rule, differences of connections are module endomorphisms, and curvature is an endomorphism-valued commutator corrected by the derivation Lie bracket.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The reconstruction statement is presented for compact topological spaces and a suitable commutative function algebra, while the noncommutative extension is an analogy promoted to definitions. Connections additionally depend on a chosen Lie algebra of derivations; this choice is part of the geometry and cannot be suppressed.
accepted_units.title: Translate geometric roles into algebraic modules and operators
accepted_units.why_material: It gives a coherent representation-change recipe that preserves roles rather than notation: identify which algebraic objects play points/functions, bundles/sections, directions, covariant differentiation, affine variation, and curvature.

accepted_units.context_note: For a noncommutative torus algebra, the compactification covariance relation is rewritten exactly as the Leibniz relation for a connection on a projective module. The source then organizes the classification problem into three steps: choose the module, compute its endomorphism algebra, and choose one connection; every general configuration is the base connection plus arbitrary endomorphism-valued terms.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on the chosen noncommutative-torus relations, derivations, projectivity of the module, and an identified base connection. The physical matrix coordinates are only one application of the algebraic connection equation, and existence/classification results are deferred to cited work.
accepted_units.title: Reframe covariance constraints as an affine space of connections
accepted_units.why_material: This separates discrete structural choices from continuous freedom: first select the carrier module, then expose all remaining solutions as a translate of its endomorphism algebra, making equivalence and gauge questions more tractable.

accepted_units.context_note: After selecting a smooth completion, involution, trace, and invariant derivations, projective modules receive Hermitian metrics and compatible connections. The endomorphism algebra of a module can be another noncommutative torus or a matrix algebra over one; the source states that it is strongly Morita equivalent to the original algebra, with a compatible trace and induced derivation action.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The geometry depends materially on the smooth completion, star structure, invariant trace, Hermitian metric, projective module, and compatibility conditions. Strong Morita equivalence preserves module-theoretic structure but is not literal algebra isomorphism, and higher-dimensional endomorphism algebras may have matrix factors.
accepted_units.title: Treat an endomorphism algebra as an equivalent geometry without identifying it literally
accepted_units.why_material: It is a disciplined duality pattern: pass from an algebra to the endomorphisms of a suitable module, transport trace and derivations, and use Morita equivalence to state what structural information is preserved while retaining representation differences.

accepted_units.context_note: In the two-dimensional case, the source invokes a classification of projective modules and constant-curvature compatible connections. Direct sums of a basic module yield block-diagonal connections, and gauge-equivalence classes of constant-curvature connections form a symmetric-product moduli space; the statement is said to persist across rational and irrational deformation parameters despite differences in module classification.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: This unit is restricted to the two-dimensional noncommutative torus and relies on results cited rather than proved in the source. The symmetric-product description depends on repeated copies of the stated basic module, compatibility, constant curvature, and quotient by gauge equivalence; rational parameters have additional modules.
accepted_units.title: Build a moduli space by quotienting repeated irreducible choices by permutation
accepted_units.why_material: It exhibits a reusable construction: when a solution decomposes into indistinguishable elementary blocks, parameters form a product before equivalence and a symmetric product after forgetting the ordering of those blocks.

accepted_units.context_note: The dimension of a projective module is defined through the trace of a representing projection and alternatively through asymptotic generator growth. K-theory records virtual module classes with a positive cone selecting actual modules. Although dimension can be nonintegral, integrated curvature remains quantized because it computes a Fredholm index.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The numerical formulas and positive cone are specific to the two-dimensional noncommutative torus and its normalized trace. Equality of the two dimension descriptions and the curvature-index relation rely on established operator-algebraic and index-theoretic results not derived here.
accepted_units.title: Separate continuous size from discrete topological charge
accepted_units.why_material: This is a useful conceptual distinction: an invariant measuring size may vary continuously under deformation while a different invariant stays quantized because it factors through an index, so nonintegral dimension does not imply loss of discrete topology.

accepted_units.context_note: The source marks the K-theory lattice, maps it into cyclic homology, and represents the algebra through a foliation and transversal. Passing to the commutant endomorphism algebra of a module gives a Morita-equivalent algebra and transports the marking, producing a modular action by fractional-linear transformations. A second modular action arises from the odd K-group and flat metrics; the two actions commute and preserve a boundary relation between their parameter spaces.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The construction is specific to marked two-dimensional noncommutative tori and uses cyclic homology, Chern character, foliations, transversals, Morita equivalence, and both K-groups. Several canonicality and reconstruction claims are summarized without local proof, and rational parameters require adding a boundary point.
accepted_units.title: Define duality on marked invariants and check compatibility of symmetry actions
accepted_units.why_material: It provides a generic recipe for controlled duality: mark the invariant lattice, transport it functorially across an equivalence object, derive the parameter action, and verify whether independently defined symmetry actions commute and preserve their incidence relation.

accepted_units.context_note: Elements of the dual noncommutative torus are represented by ordinary functions on a commutative torus, while algebra multiplication is transferred to a star product. Commutators become Moyal-type brackets, and an algebraic derivation becomes ordinary differentiation in this representation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The identification uses a chosen Fourier basis, phase convention, constant deformation parameter, and the particular two-torus algebra. Exact exponential differential operators, signs, and normalization are OCR-sensitive; the subsequent gauge-theory action is not part of this generic unit.
accepted_units.title: Move noncommutativity from objects into the multiplication law
accepted_units.why_material: It is a reusable representation change: keep the underlying function space familiar but deform composition, then translate algebraic commutators and derivations into bracket and differential operations while tracking which structures changed.

ecosystem_findings.summary: The source grounds a disciplined duality pattern in which a module's commutant becomes a Morita-equivalent geometry and marked K-theory is transported to define modular actions. The assignment supplied the lens identifier; parent-corpus overlap and external novelty were not assessed.

The source repeatedly preserves structural roles while moving among spaces, function algebras, projective modules, connection operators, and ordinary functions with deformed multiplication. This is source-grounded support for the assignment-routed lens, not a claim of novelty or independent correctness.

The source does not clearly ground projectivization as a generic move: its `projective` objects are direct-summand modules, while `compactification` is principally a physics boundary condition. Those notions should not be conflated or forced into one lens without separate evidence; novelty and relation to the frozen parent remain unconfirmed.
